answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a plume as the anchor of the cost. A juniper stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a velvet holds...
